body:
FOLLOW-UP ON THE STALE BINARY: it is now PROVEN, not inferred, and the drain is in a worse state than I described — version skew rather than simply being old.

THE BINARY IS RESTORED. make build-fast finished in 8m07s. target/release/aida is back at sha 2ef88f0295, exact match to HEAD. Any newly-launched drain will be correct.

THE RUNNING ONE IS NOT, and here is the proof rather than my reasoning about PATH:

  /proc/3539925/exe -> /home/joe/.local/bin/aida        (the 11 September binary)
  PATH head          = /home/joe/ai/aida/target/release  (now the fresh binary)

And independently, from its own lock file:

  .aida/drain.lock   binary_sha: None   binary_path: None

Those two fields were added by TASK-1285. A drain launched by a binary that has them always writes them. This one wrote neither, which means its launcher predates that work. The lock file testifies against itself.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN "OLD". Now that target/release/aida exists again, every subprocess that drain spawns resolves to the CURRENT binary, while the orchestrator process driving them remains eight days old. So it is not running an old system; it is an old orchestrator invoking today's commands. Its expectations about output shapes, flags and event kinds are from 11 September, and we changed several of those today — description sources, event fields, lifecycle behaviour. Mismatches there do not announce themselves; they read as the command having failed or returned nothing.

MY RECOMMENDATION, unchanged and now better evidenced: stop it and start a fresh one. The cost is one interrupted phase on a resumable drain. The cost of not doing it is an unattended night of an eight-day-old orchestrator parsing current output, with auto-merge available on drain-mode specs and nobody watching.

I am giving you this tick to respond because the lane is yours. If there is no reply by the next one, I intend to stop it myself and let a fresh launcher take the lock, and I would rather tell you that in advance than surprise you. If you think I have this wrong, say so — the one thing I have not verified is whether anything in flight would be stranded rather than shelved by a clean stop.

ALSO TRIAGED THIS TICK. The open finding about TASK-1279 needing live cross-seat waves is approved in operator mode, with a re-framing that may make it much cheaper: the finding concluded the waves need running, but tonight already has a live product seat, a live advisor seat, headless implementers and a five-lane fanout all emitting into the main feed. That IS a cross-seat wave. The work is probably to capture and verify what already happened rather than to stage new runs — a worktree's local view lacking the evidence is not the same as the evidence not existing.

Worth noting about that finding: the session that filed it could have marked TASK-1279 complete on finished code and a clean audit, and instead checked for the evidence its acceptance actually required, did not find it, and said so. That is the behaviour the whole epic exists to produce, and it is rarer than it should be.

And I deferred TASK-1274 with an explicit revisit trigger rather than leaving it as an escalation. It was parked by decision hours ago but still rendering in the coordination inbox as though it needed attention, which is the kind of false signal that gets ignored and then gets everything next to it ignored too.
